notes:
ACCESS: plain requests = HTTP 403; curl_cffi impersonate=chrome131 returned 200 on every URL (the same route the prior Home-Decor pass used). No proxy needed, no WAF workaround, no Claude-specific robots disallow involved.
TREE: taken from the site's own /catalog/sitemap page (full department -> section -> node listing, 235 catalog links) and cross-checked against the schema.org SiteNavigationElement mega-menu graph embedded in every page (script class='schema-top-menu-data'). Every candidate node was opened and its __NEXT_DATA__ read. R&B's page model self-identifies the level: props.pageProps.documentType = 'INTERMEDIATE_CATEGORY' for a pure grouping page (no productGroups at all), 'STANDARD' for a real listing, 'EDITORIAL' for a curated landing page. Every INTERMEDIATE_CATEGORY node (Sofas & Sectionals, Chairs & Ottomans, Accent Tables, Living Storage, Dining Tables, Dining Seating, Dining & Kitchen Storage, Beds & Mattresses, Bedroom Furniture, Bath Furniture, Storage By Type, Entryway, Desks & Chairs, Office Systems, Office Storage & Organization, Outdoor Lounge, Outdoor Accent Tables, Dining & Outdoor Kitchen, Custom Sectionals, Custom Tables) is a parent with extractable children and was NOT recorded as a leaf. I emitted one grouping level - the department - because R&B's actual mega-menu is flat under each department; the intermediate section headers (Tables / Seating / Storage / Furniture) exist only on the site-map page and several of them repeat verbatim across departments, which would have produced ambiguous duplicate grouping rows.
QTY METHOD: Room & Board publishes NO 'N items' header anywhere on a PLP and exposes no count API (verified by stripping scripts/tags and regexing every page for 'N items|products|results' - the only hits were product option strings such as '5 items, 2 leg finishes'). Each PLP server-renders its ENTIRE listing with no pagination, so every qty is a full enumeration, taken from props.pageProps.document.productGroups and independently cross-verified against the number of '"@type":"Product"' entries in the same page's server-rendered JSON-LD. The two agreed EXACTLY on all 61 STANDARD listings. Sanity checks: the number changes per category (no constant site-wide total); no suspiciously round values; a second read of six categories (living/chairs 90, living/ottomans 77, bedroom/beds 46, office/desks 34, outdoor-dining-tables 23, storage-cabinets 40) returned identical numbers, so no session drift; each page's h1/longName was confirmed to match the node requested. qty counts product TILES (product groups), which is exactly what the shopper sees on the grid; a few tiles share an internal family id (e.g. Aria / Decker / Glover Tables each appear as three shape tiles) but names and URLs are all distinct, so the tile count is the honest grid count.
DE-DUPLICATION: R&B surfaces several product-type listings under multiple departments with different paths but byte-identical product sets (verified by comparing product-group id sets). I resolved each to the site's own document.canonicalUrl and recorded it exactly once: Storage Cabinets (40), Media Cabinets (16) and Bookcases & Wall Units (44) canonicalise to /catalog/storage-and-entryway/...; Bar Cabinets & Carts (18) to /catalog/dining-and-kitchen/...; Benches & Stools (54) and Consoles (36) to /catalog/living/...; Coat Racks (16) to /catalog/storage-and-entryway/.... Dropped as exact duplicates: the living/dining/bedroom/office variants of bookcases-and-wall-units, the living/dining variants of storage-cabinets, the living/storage-and-entryway variants of bar-cabinets-and-carts, bedroom + storage-and-entryway benches-and-stools, storage-and-entryway consoles, living media-cabinets, and office coat-racks. Kept as genuinely different listings (self-canonical, different product sets): office/storage-cabinets (22, only 2 tiles shared with the 40) and bath/benches-and-stools (11).
EXCLUDED and why: Mattresses, and 'Adjustable Beds & Platform Board' (4 tiles: two adjustable bed bases, a platform board, a box spring - mattress foundations, not furniture). Bath > 'Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets' (35) - primary product type is mirrors, which belongs to Wall Decor; the bathroom cabinetry is separately captured by Bath Storage (linen + medicine cabinets). All lighting, rugs, textiles, bedding, wall art, mirrors, picture frames, vases, planters, candles, tabletop, kitchen tools, care & cleaning, baskets & bins, trays & small storage, hooks & wall organizers, wall shelves & ledges, cabinet hardware, bath hardware / organization / linens / laundry / self-care, outdoor cushions, patio umbrellas, furniture covers, outdoor care products, desktop organizers and power outlets. EDITORIAL landing / 'pairings' pages dropped per the no-collections rule: Table & Chair Pairings, Favorite Outdoor Lounge Combos, Favorite Outdoor Dining Combos, Home Office Combinations, Custom & Modular Storage (a landing page re-presenting bookcases and wall units already recorded), Bath Storage & Organization; also New Living (new arrivals) and all /clearance/ nodes. The one EDITORIAL page kept is Bedroom > Bunk & Loft Beds, a genuine kids-furniture category node in the nav with no STANDARD equivalent - see its flag.
OVERLAPS kept transparently rather than silently merged: Outdoor Benches (6) contains the 4 Outdoor Dining Benches; the Made for You custom tables / desks / sectionals share 0 tiles with their standard counterparts (checked by product-group id), but Custom Storage Cabinets & Bookcases shares 6 of its 9 with Storage Cabinets (40).
